data.narrative: The student applied a five-category review, then traced a high-risk team invitation path through controller, live role guard, and transactional service code. The reflection separates source-level safeguards from unexecuted PostgreSQL-backed HTTP cases and records a reproducible whitespace/diff check without overstating runtime proof.

dimension_scores.observation: The review work used focused criteria across five failure categories and a concrete team-scoped IDOR scenario.
dimension_scores.evidence: review-pass.md records Security, Edge Cases, Error Handling, Naming, and Tests findings; idor-fix-verification.md specifies the principalId + teamId authorization contract and expected 201/403 cases.

dimension_scores.observation: The student followed the high-risk path through route, UUID validation, authenticated identity, live role lookup, and transaction-backed writes.
dimension_scores.evidence: idor-fix-verification.md reviews teams.controller.ts, team-role.guard.ts, and teams.service.ts line by line and distinguishes actor authorization from invitee membership checks.

dimension_scores.observation: The student used a broad risk pass to target deeper inspection and ran one bounded verification check rather than making unrelated edits.
dimension_scores.evidence: The reflection records git diff --check exit 0, all four requested review artifacts present, zero trailing-whitespace findings, and no changes to src/teams/ or prisma/.

dimension_scores.observation: The student correctly treated code inspection as source evidence and withheld runtime claims when the database was unavailable.
dimension_scores.evidence: Both required authorization scenarios are explicitly marked NOT EXECUTED because PostgreSQL at 127.0.0.1:5432 was unreachable; expected statuses are labeled as source-derived.

dimension_scores.observation: The reflection connects the review method, source evidence, verification limits, and a practical next validation step.
dimension_scores.evidence: module-04-reflection.md documents the review trade-offs and specifies authorized/denied requests plus database write assertions for a future run against url_shortener_test.

strengths: Connects broad failure-category review to targeted line-by-line investigation of the high-risk authorization path.
Identifies live team-scoped role enforcement and parameterized transactional writes from source evidence.
Clearly separates expected behavior from database-backed HTTP results that were not executed.
data.recommendation: When PostgreSQL for url_shortener_test is reachable, run the authorized OWNER/ADMIN and denied member/non-member invitation cases, assert 201 and 403, and verify that denial leaves no invitation, audit, or activity records.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: The review followed principalId and teamId into the live team_members lookup and checked the OWNER/ADMIN role gate.
The student distinguished source-level behavior from unexecuted database-backed HTTP outcomes.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the invitation controller, role guard, and service as a concrete trace of the IDOR boundary.
Started with five review categories, selected the high-risk authorization path, and followed its data and checks.

learning_style_signals: Uses exact file/line evidence and command results to distinguish verified behavior from assumptions.

public_evidence.artifact: Module 04 critical review and IDOR verification notes
public_evidence.student_action: Reviewed the team invitation authorization path and documented source evidence, expected outcomes, and runtime verification limits.
public_evidence.technical_detail: The role guard binds the authenticated principal and team ID in a parameterized team_members query and restricts the route to OWNER or ADMIN.
public_evidence.proof: The four prior review artifacts passed git diff --check; all were present with zero trailing-whitespace findings. PostgreSQL-backed HTTP cases remain marked NOT EXECUTED.
public_evidence.ability: Reviews security-sensitive code with evidence-calibrated conclusions.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student can identify an authorization boundary and avoid presenting static review as runtime proof.
